what: Which of the three candidate mechanisms of Issue #186 produces the post-combat clinch, decided by counting how many refused steps each of them could have prevented, and the decision that follows.
question: Issue #186, criterion 3: «Назван виновный механизм, и решение о том, чинить его здесь или поднимать #76, принято явно и с числом».

howItWasMeasured.sample: 782 refused steps by ex-combatants inside the 60 ticks after a wave ended, over 13 measured windows of the seed matrix, 3780 cohort creature-ticks.
howItWasMeasured.howTheBlockerIsIdentified: The tile the refused step was for is not published, so it is recomputed by the simulation's own rule — the same BFS over the same passable tiles, neighbours visited north, east, south, west, first shortest path wins. The eligibility of whoever stands on it is then rebuilt from the snapshot the way PrototypeWorld.CanYield asks it: not Fighting, not Downed, no meal reserved, not mustering, and not already standing on its own destination.
howItWasMeasured.whatThisCannotSee: The rebuilt eligibility is a model of CanYield and not CanYield itself: a mutant of the simulation's own CanYield would not move these counts. That is named here rather than left to be discovered — the number is an upper bound on what a yield could buy, computed from published state, and it is used as an upper bound below.

candidates.candidate: the choice of destination after the fight (the approach rule of Issue #129)
candidates.reachOfTheFix: not a way of clearing a refused step at all
candidates.number: It changes how many creatures are standing in one room when the fight ends, and by how much is in evidence/186-before-after-129.json: refused steps per cohort creature-tick 0.147 -> 0.207 (×1.40), refused steps towards a tile a neighbour wants on the same tick 10 -> 186 (×18.6), most ex-combatants refused a step together on one tick 4 -> 6. What it does not change is the share of refused steps with a way round: 0.916 -> 0.931.
candidates.verdict: amplifier, not mechanism. Reverting it is a non-goal of the Issue and would not remove the jam, only thin the crowd standing in it.

candidates.number: 307 refused steps (39.3 %) were blocked by a creature standing on its own destination, which CanYield refuses to order aside by rule, and 54 more (6.9 %) by a creature with a meal reserved or mustering, which it also refuses unless the block is a proven dependency cycle — 361 (46.2 %) out of reach of a yield by design. Of the 328 blocked by a creature a yield may move, 327 had an empty tile beside them to be moved onto. On 680 of 782 ticks (87.0 %) no chosen_traffic_yield was planned anywhere in the world at all.
candidates.verdict: the weakest of the three. Its ceiling is under half the sample, and the largest single class of refused steps is one it is designed never to touch.

candidates.candidate: the absence of tile occupancy in pathfinding (Issue #76)
candidates.number: On 728 refused steps a route to the same destination existed within 4 extra steps once every other creature counted as a wall, and on 516 of those (66.0 % of the whole sample) that route was strictly longer than the one PrototypeMap.NextStep hands out — a different route, not the same one re-derived. Only 24 refused steps (3.1 %) had no route at all: the creature is almost never walled in, it is standing in front of a tile somebody is on with an empty tile beside it.
candidates.verdict: the mechanism. A way round reaches 728 refused steps where a yield reaches at most 327 — more than twice as many, which is what PrototypePostCombatDispersalTests.Walking_round_reaches_more_of_the_clinch_than_a_yield_could holds.

theDecision.what: Not fixed here. This raises Issue #76.
theDecision.onWhatNumber: 728 against 327: the mechanism that reaches 93.1 % of the refused steps is tile occupancy in the pathfinder, and the Issue names implementing it a non-goal — «не реализовывать занятость клетки в этой задаче: если измерение покажет, что причина там, это поднимает #76». The measurement showed it is there.
theDecision.whyNotAPartialFixOfTheArbitrationInstead: Its ceiling is 41.8 % of the sample and its floor is the 46.2 % it may not touch by rule. Tuning it here would be work against a symptom whose dominant cause is one method away, and it would move the corridors of 13.4 for a gain that the same measurement bounds in advance.
whatIssue76HasToAnswerWhenItIsTaken: a BFS that treats bodies as walls has no route at all on 24 of 782 refused steps, so the rule needs an answer for the enclosed case that is not «stand still forever»
the yield arbitration stays necessary for exactly those, and its rule about who may be told to step aside does not change

the morale rule of 10.3 counts bodies and not tiles («семеро на одном тайле дают семь»), and raiders assign their position with no occupancy check at all — making a raider hold a tile is a separate decision, already named in evidence/129-before.json

theOtherHalfOfTheSymptom.what: The larger half of what the owner saw is not a clinch and is not Issue #76.
theOtherHalfOfTheSymptom.number: 1989 of 3780 cohort creature-ticks (52.6 %) passed with neither a step nor a refused step; 1121 of them (29.7 % of the window) in CreatureMode.Waiting. The commonest last decision of such a creature is waiting_stock_sufficient, 850 times. On baseline/20260728 wave 1 seven of eight ex-combatants never left the tile the fight ended on in 60 ticks, with 0 refused steps in the whole window. Per cohort-tick this half barely moved with #129: 0.283 before, 0.297 after.
theOtherHalfOfTheSymptom.whyItIsNotDecidedHere: A creature with no work stands where it is standing, and after a fight that is the middle of the fight. Giving it somewhere to go is new behaviour, not a defect fix: it is a gameplay decision about what an ex-combatant with nothing to do does, and AGENTS.md sends those to the owner. It is named here and returned rather than taken.
